changing the type of training to keep it interesting and effective
tips: An interesting development in recent years is that some developed countries are starting to see reductions in their energy use per person, which includes the UK and Canada. Students could explore reasons (e.g. energy efficiency, vehicle electrification) and consider whether this trend will continue.

4086.name: Distribution of oil reserves, factors affecting growth of oil consumption
4086.outcome: I can explain how oil reserves and production are unevenly distributed and that oil consumption is increasing.
points: The global demand for oil is increasing.
Oil reserves and production are unevenly distributed.
Oil consumption is growing due to rising per capita GDP and rapid industrialisation in emerging countries.
keywords: nations with social or business activities in the process of rapid growth and industrialisation
where a mainly agricultural society changes and begins to depend more on manufacturing industries
locations where oil is found in significant amounts
tips: Interestingly, as development increases, countries use more energy and oil. That is, until the country reaches a high level of development whereby oil consumption falls off. Students could explore reasons for this (e.g. energy efficiency, vehicle electrification, rise of renewable energy).

4087.name: Changing oil supply and prices
4087.outcome: I can explain how changing international relations and economic factors can affect oil supply and oil prices.
points: Oil production and the price of oil change over time.
Political factors, such as conflicts and changing diplomatic relations, affect oil supply and oil prices.
Economic factors, such as recessions and booms and under and over supply, affect oil supply and oil prices.
keywords: a measure of how much of something people want to buy
how well (or badly) countries get along with each other, which can affect trading relationships of supply and demand
a period when economies stop growing temporarily and people spend less
the amount of something that is available to buy
tips: Practising interpreting oil price and oil production data is a very useful skill for students to develop, and can usually be linked to current news events.

guidance.label: Depiction or discussion of violence or suffering
guidance.description: Depiction of war, threats of war, death or the aftermath of war.

4088.name: Developing conventional oil/gas sources in sensitive or remote areas
4088.outcome: I can explain the economic costs and benefits of developing conventional sources of oil and gas in ecologically-sensitive and isolated areas.
points: The world’s continuing reliance on fossil fuels increases pressure to exploit new areas.
There are economic benefits of developing conventional oil and gas sources in ecologically-sensitive and isolated areas.
There are economic costs of developing conventional oil and gas sources in ecologically-sensitive and isolated areas.
keywords: If you are conventional, you follow accepted norms or standards.
a known amount of oil or gas that can be taken from underground and used
tips: Using Google Earth or similar applications to really demonstrate the remoteness of sites like ExxonMobil's Point Thomson reservoir helps students to grasp the logistical difficulties involved in extracting oil and gas from Alaska's North Slope.

4090.name: Developing unconventional oil/gas sources in sensitive or remote areas
4090.outcome: I can explain the environmental costs associated with developing unconventional sources of oil and gas - oil from tar sands and gas from shale.
points: Unconventional sources of oil and gas include shale gas and tar sands.
Unconventional sources of oil and gas are increasingly being exploited.
There are environmental costs associated with developing new unconventional oil and gas sources.
keywords: If you are unconventional, you do not follow accepted norms or standards.
whether what is in a supply of water (e.g. its chemical or biological contents) make it suitable for a particular kind of use
tips: Watching a video to show the processes involved in converting tar sands to oil and extracting gas from shale rocks can help students understand the challenges involved in making use of unconventional oil and gas sources.

4091.name: Reducing demand on fossil fuels
4091.outcome: I can explain how energy efficiency and energy conservation in transport and in the home can reduce demand for finite energy resources and reduce carbon emissions.
points: Reducing reliance on fossil fuels presents major technical challenges.
Energy efficiency and conservation can reduce demand and help finite energy supplies to last longer.
Energy efficiency and energy conservation can help to reduce carbon emissions.
keywords: protection and management of natural resources to prevent damage and maintain biodiversity
a measure of how much of something people want to buy
working in an organised way that doesn't waste time and resources
tips: Students could carry out a review of energy efficient technology in the school and make suggestions for how energy conservation could be improved within the school day.

4092.name: Costs and benefits to fossil fuel alternatives
4092.outcome: I can assess the costs and benefits of alternatives to fossil fuels.
points: The UK's energy mix has diversified in response to policies of reducing carbon emissions and improving energy security.
2020 was the UK's first year in which more electricity came from alternatives to fossil fuels than from non-renewables.
Alternatives to fossil fuels can reduce carbon emissions, improve energy security and diversify the energy mix.
Alternatives to fossil fuels include biofuels, wind, solar, HEP and future technologies such as hydrogen.
Alternatives to fossil fuels have both benefits and costs.
keywords: the total amount of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere by an individual, product, process, country, etc
the combination of different energy sources used by a country or a region. The energy mix can change over time
the uninterrupted availability of energy sources at an affordable price
tips: The UK's National Grid: Live service (grid.iamkate.com) provides a dashboard of live data on the UK's electricity generation and consumption, which could be a useful resource for students to explore in relation to energy mix and alternatives to fossil fuels.

4093.name: Energy futures – contrasting views
4093.outcome: I can explain why different groups have contrasting views about energy futures.
points: Energy futures are different possible ways in which energy might be produced, consumed and managed in the future.
Different groups have contrasting views about energy futures.
keywords: different scenarios about ways in which energy might be produced, consumed and managed in the future
balancing the amount of greenhouse gases emitted into the atmosphere with the amount removed from it
tips: The Royal Meteorological Society and Royal Geographical Society have produced resources based on the IPCC climate change report for 2021/22 which, though aimed at A level students, provide great resources for investigating this topic at GCSE, too.

4094.name: Changing attitudes to unsustainable energy consumption
4094.outcome: I can explain ways in which attitudes to unsustainable energy consumption are changing.
points: A carbon footprint is the total greenhouse gas emissions caused directly and indirectly by an individual or activity.
In some developed countries, there are changing attitudes to unsustainable energy consumption.
Environmental concerns, economic interests and education are responsible for changing attitudes.
keywords: the total amount of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere by an individual, product, process, country, etc
the impact of a person or community on the environment, expressed as the amount of land required to sustain their use of natural resources
balancing the amount of greenhouse gases emitted into the atmosphere with the amount removed from it
tips: There are several carboon footprint and ecological footprint calculators online, such as the WWF Footprint Calculator and the Global Footprint Network Calculator.

4096.name: Making a geographical decision
4096.outcome: I can evaluate different sources of evidence to justify a decision about a geographical issue.
points: Geographical issues link different parts of geography together and involve decisions about how land is used.
There is a wide range of data that can be used when evaluating geographical issues, including graphs and maps.
Data can be used to understand issue and as evidence to support an argument.
Geographers use evidence to make decisions and aim to balance the needs of people and the environment.
keywords: Context concerns the circumstances in which a text was written; context helps us to understand the writer’s intentions further.
GDP plus income from foreign investments and remittances, divided by the population
an area with a very high number of different species, many of which are found nowhere else
a natural or artificial system that absorbs more carbon dioxide than it releases
tips: This lesson provides a framework to help students understand and engage with the decision making element of paper 3. Teachers may want to use this as an introduction to decision making or break up and use different parts of the lesson separately.

3236.belief: Geography is learning about the natural world.
3236.statement: Geography is learning about the natural world.
3236.correction: Geography has many different aspects and includes learning about the natural world and learning about society.

4456.correction: Different maps aim to show different things such as country borders, the location of physical features and the height of the land.

2381.belief: Digital maps are only used to locate places.
2381.statement: Digital maps are only used to locate places.
2381.correction: Digital maps are used in many different jobs and used to present data.

4045.belief: Latitude lines run vertically down the Earth.
4045.statement: Latitude lines run vertically down the Earth.
4045.correction: Latitude lines run horizontally while longitude lines run vertically.

4457.belief: Maps always have the same symbols.
4457.statement: Maps always have the same symbols.
4457.correction: You find different symbols depending on the scale of your map.

2024.belief: Contours are only used to show hills and mountains.
2024.statement: Contours are only used to show hills and mountains.
2024.correction: Contours are used to show the height of the land at 10 metre intervals above sea level.

5255.belief: OS maps all use the same scale.
5255.statement: OS maps all use the same scale.

2967.belief: Fieldwork must take place in an unfamiliar location.
2967.statement: Fieldwork must take place in an unfamiliar location.
2967.correction: While it can be exciting to do fieldwork in a new place, fieldwork actually can take place anywhere.

8674.belief: The purpose of data presentation is to make the data more attractive.
8674.statement: The purpose of data presentation is to make the data more attractive.
8674.correction: The purpose of data presentation is to allow geographers to identify patterns and relationships in the data.

10013.belief: Subjective data is automatically invalid and should be ignored.
10013.statement: Subjective data is automatically invalid and should be ignored.
10013.correction: Geographers use subjective data a lot as they value people's, and their own, opinion about something.

8372.belief: Weather and climate are the same.
8372.statement: Pupils may think that weather and climate are the same.
8372.correction: Pupils will explore that weather is the short term changes in the atmosphere whereas climate is long term changes in the atmospheric patterns of a place.

1750.belief: It is always colder at the coast because it is near water.
1750.statement: It is always colder at the coast because it is near water.
1750.correction: Students will understand that, in winter, coastal areas tend to be warmer because water takes longer to heat up.

10523.belief: The UK’s climate is the same across the country.
10523.statement: The UK’s climate is the same across the country.
10523.correction: Students will understand that the UK’s climate varies between different regions due to latitude, altitude and air masses.

368.belief: Areas of high wind speeds are colder.
368.statement: Areas of high wind speeds are colder.
368.correction: While windy areas may feel colder on our bodies, geographers measure air temperature which is unlikely to be affected by the strength of the wind speed.

4494.belief: It does not matter which aspects of the data are presented on which axis of a graph.
4494.statement: It does not matter which aspects of the data are presented on which axis of a graph.
4494.correction: It is a common convention for the independent variable to be read from the x-axis and the dependent variable to be read from the y-axis.

478.belief: Assumptions and interpretations in geographical analysis are equally valid.
478.statement: Assumptions and interpretations in geographical analysis are equally valid.
478.correction: Geographers should always aim to interpret their data accurately rather than make assumptions about it.

5167.belief: There is only one type of rain; it is all the same.
5167.statement: There is only one type of rain; it is all the same.
5167.correction: Students will be exposed to the three different types of rainfall: relief, convectional, frontal.

10957.belief: The weather associated with an anticyclone stays the same all year around.
10957.statement: The weather associated with an anticyclone stays the same all year around.
10957.correction: Students will analyse images to identify how anticyclones may bring different weather in the summer and winter.

10961.belief: Weather forecasts are only seen on apps and on the TV. Weather forecasts just use symbols.
10961.statement: Weather forecasts are only seen on apps and on the TV. Weather forecasts just use symbols.
10961.correction: Students will explore synoptic charts, used by meteorologists, to interpret the weather.

1709.belief: Climate change and global warming are the same thing.
1709.statement: Climate change and global warming are the same thing.
1709.correction: Global warming is the increase in Earth's average temperature over a long period of time, whereas climate change is a large-scale and long-term change in the planet’s climate, including weather patterns and average temperatures.

1708.belief: Climate change is entirely caused by humans.
1708.statement: Climate change is entirely caused by humans.
1708.correction: Students will recognise that our climate changes naturally and there are physical causes of this. Humans have intensified the process in recent years.

1716.belief: Climate change simply means hotter, drier summers in the UK.
1716.statement: Climate change simply means hotter, drier summers in the UK.
1716.correction: Warmer temperatures in summer and fewer cold spells in winter are due to climate change. There is also some evidence that the UK is also experiencing more heavy rain events.

3892.belief: It's fine to adapt or mitigate, we don't need to do both.
3892.statement: It's fine to adapt or mitigate, we don't need to do both.
3892.correction: Adaptation helps us cope with climate change, but it doesn’t stop the problem from getting worse. Mitigation helps slow down climate change. The best approach is to use both mitigation and adaptation.

675.belief: Birth rates and death rates are the total number of people who have been born or died.
675.statement: That birth rates and death rates are the total number of people who have been born or died.
675.correction: Birth and death rates are per 1 000 people per year.

5705.belief: Population density is the same everywhere.
5705.statement: Population density is the same everywhere.
5705.correction: This misconception arises because students may not realise that geographical factors vary widely. Address this by comparing different regions.

3302.belief: GIS web maps are only a tool for visualising geographical patterns in data; they can't help us explain geographical patterns.
3302.statement: GIS web maps are only a tool for visualising geographical patterns in data; they can't help us explain geographical patterns.
3302.correction: GIS are a useful tool to visualise, interpret and analyse geographical data. This means they can be used to explain geographical patterns by comparing different layers.

5704.belief: Population density is the same across the UK.
5704.statement: Population density is the same across the UK.
5704.correction: Population density varies widely due to factors like topography and urbanisation.

5708.correction: Population pyramids can have different shapes depending on demographic factors. Some may be more rectangular or even inverted, reflecting various population structures.

3301.belief: GIS can only show one set of data.
3301.statement: GIS can only show one set of data.
3301.correction: GIS can show multiple layers of data as well as change over time.

4610.correction: Not all migrants are refugees; some move for economic or educational reasons. Explain the differences between refugees and other migrants.

4617.correction: Migration also brings benefits such as skills and expertise for the jobs market, economic benefits and a more diverse society.

4613.correction: Migration brings other cultures, foods and fashion to the UK.

2069.correction: Not all countries have ageing populations. It is more common in higher income nations with longer life expectancies.

5288.belief: Overpopulation and underpopulation are only about the number of people in a country.
5288.statement: Overpopulation and underpopulation are only about the number of people in a country.
5288.correction: It’s not just about numbers—it’s about how well a country’s resources match the needs of its population.

11127.belief: World population increses equally across the globe.
11127.statement: World population increses equally across the globe.
11127.correction: Population is expected to increase in some parts of the world but in other areas the population is expected to decrease.

1738.statement: That all coastlines are sandy beaches.
1738.correction: Not all coastlines are sandy beaches. Some coastlines have beaches of stones called shingle, and some coastlines only have cliffs without any beach.

10938.belief: Waves and tides are the same thing, or that tides are the cause of waves, or that wind causes both waves and tides.
10938.statement: That waves and tides are the same thing, or that tides are the cause of waves, or that wind causes both waves and tides.
10938.correction: Waves are caused by the wind blowing across the sea, not by the tide. The tide is the regular rise and fall of the sea level regardless of whether there are waves or if the sea is calm.

9754.statement: Students frequently mix up the different types of processes, their names and definitions.
9754.correction: Flag up words for processes that sound similar or have similar spellings as you encounter them. Signpost the differences in their meanings, and encourage students to highlight them in a way that is most useful for them, for example by colour coding.

9942.belief: Soft rock is physically soft to the touch, like a pillow.
9942.statement: Students may think that soft rock is physically soft to the touch, like a pillow.
9942.correction: Geologically soft is not the same as being soft like a pillow. All rock feels solid when touched, even soft rocks. Rock that is classified as soft, like clay, can crumble and break more easily than rock which is classified as hard, like granite.

2403.belief: The direction of the prevailing wind is the direction that the wind is blowing in at any particular time.
2403.statement: That the direction of the prevailing wind is the direction that the wind is blowing in at any particular time.
2403.correction: The prevailing wind is wind from a particular direction that is most frequently experienced in a location. Winds can come from other directions, especially in stormy conditions, but they are not the same as the prevailing wind.

1707.belief: Climate change causes global warming, or that climate change and global warming are the same thing.
1707.statement: That climate change causes global warming, or that climate change and global warming are the same thing.
1707.correction: Global warming is the rise in average temperatures as a result of the greenhouse effect. Climate change is changes to weather patterns (including temperatures and rainfall patterns) as a result of global warming.

1734.belief: Coastal erosion is likely to be the same in different places along a stretch of coastline.
1734.statement: Coastal erosion is likely to be the same in different places along a stretch of coastline.
1734.correction: Coastal erosion varies between different places. It is influenced by human factors, such as whether coastal defences have been installed, and physical factors, such as the rock type.

9845.statement: Students may think that coastal defences stop erosion entirely.
9845.correction: Coastal defences aim to protect the coastline from erosion, and can greatly reduce erosion but they can't stop it completely. Defences don't last forever, so eventually the power of the sea will regain strength in areas previously protected.

2807.belief: Everyone involved or invested in a plan must want said coastal management project to happen to protect the coastline of an area.
2807.statement: That everyone involved or invested in a plan must want said coastal management project to happen to protect the coastline of an area.
2807.correction: In almost all cases, there are a wide range of opinions about coastal management projects, some in support of the plans and others not in favour for various reasons that they feel are important.

9964.belief: All water is the same, or can mix up saltwater (seawater) and freshwater and where these are found.
9964.statement: Students can think that all water is the same, or can mix up saltwater (seawater) and freshwater and where these are found.
9964.correction: Water on Earth is either saltwater or freshwater. Saltwater is found in seas and oceans, freshwater is found in rivers and streams. Only salt tolerant plants and animal species can survive in saltwater.

9145.belief: Sea level is constantly the same and that elevation is the same as height in general.
9145.statement: That sea level is constantly the same and that elevation is the same as height in general.
9145.correction: Sea level changes with the tides; the measure that we use as a baseline is the mean (average) sea level. This is used to calculate elevation of geographical features; sea level is taken as zero and every 1 metre in height is 1 metre above sea level.

8969.belief: Rising sea levels only affect a few places like tropical islands, and that cities are not at risk of rising sea levels.
8969.statement: That rising sea levels only affect a few places like tropical islands, and that cities are not at risk of rising sea levels.
8969.correction: Rising sea levels is a concern for all global coastal communities. There is nowhere with a coast that will not be affected by rising sea levels, including major global cities, although some communities are affected more than others.

3095.correction: Different forests have unique characteristics and ecosystems. The boreal forest, for example, is characterised by its cold climate and coniferous trees.

10357.belief: Topical rainforests are cold and wet.
10357.statement: Topical rainforests are cold and wet.
10357.correction: In tropical rainforests it is hot, this heat actually causes the rain by creating a lot of evaporation and rising air, which then cools and condenses to form clouds which rain.

5414.belief: Only people that live in/near the rainforest use it.
5414.statement: Only people that live in/near the rainforest use it.
5414.correction: Many products grown/extracted from the rainforest are exported and used by people all over the world.

9622.belief: Stopping deforestation just means preventing the felling of trees.
9622.statement: Stopping deforestation just means preventing the felling of trees.
9622.correction: There are many approaches to preventing and even reversing deforestation not just one, for example national parks, selective logging, small-scale agroforestry and ecotourism.

8744.belief: Rainforests must have the most nutritious soil as they have such a lot of plants and such tall trees.
8744.statement: Rainforests must have the most nutritious soil as they have such a lot of plants and such tall trees.
8744.correction: Temperate deciduous forests have more nutrient rich soil than other forests as trees lose their leaves, meaning there is a lot of leaf litter and the climate is not too cold for decomposers.

292.belief: Only animals adapt to different conditions.
292.statement: Only animals adapt to different conditions.
292.correction: Many plants and animals adapt in many different ways to their surroundings.

2785.belief: Evergreen and coniferous trees are the same.
2785.statement: Evergreen and coniferous trees are the same.
2785.correction: Coniferous trees produce cones and are normally evergreen (don't lose their leaves in autumn). Some evergreen trees are not coniferous, e.g. holly.

3743.belief: All Indigenous people have a traditional lifestyle.
3743.statement: All Indigenous people have a traditional lifestyle.
3743.correction: Indigenous people may have a traditional lifestyle, e.g. reindeer herders, or may have taken on less traditional lifestyles and/or migrated.

3397.belief: The greenhouse effect has a negative impact.
3397.statement: The greenhouse effect has a negative impact.
3397.correction: The greenhouse effect is a natural process that is essential for life on Earth. Without it, our planet would be too cold to sustain most life forms.

11004.correction: Wildfires can be ignited by natural (e.g. lightning) or human causes (e.g. campfires).

8876.belief: Removing mangroves on the coast will not affect people inland or out at sea.
8876.statement: Removing mangroves on the coast will not affect people inland or out at sea.
8876.correction: Mangroves provide many services, including flood protection for settlements inland and nurseries for young fish (who may be caught for food when they have grown and left the protection of the mangroves).

3094.belief: The forests should be fenced off and guarded to stop illegal logging.
3094.statement: The forests should be fenced off and guarded to stop illegal logging.
3094.correction: Forests span far too great an area for humans to guard or fence off. Therefore technology is used to help track forests and timber.

3738.belief: India is much smaller than Greenland.
3738.statement: India is much smaller than Greenland.
3738.correction: India is similar in size to Greenland although looks much smaller on some projections of the world map.

1946.belief: Confusion about the difference between weather and climate.
1946.statement: Confusion about the difference between weather and climate.
1946.correction: The weather of a place describes the day to day conditions of the atmosphere. Climate is an average of weather conditions in a place over a long period of time (usually 30 years or more).

8748.belief: It always rains during the monsoon season.
8748.statement: It always rains during the monsoon season.
8748.correction: Explain that the rainfall intensity and frequency during the monsoon season can vary from year to year. Although it can rain every or most days, this is often a short period of intense rainfall followed by a period of dry conditions.

5503.belief: The physical geography of India doesn't vary across the country.
5503.statement: The physical geography of India doesn't vary across the country.
5503.correction: Use GIS or atlases to investigate how India's phyiscal geography varies across the country.

2827.belief: Everyone will have the same views and opinions about the importance of protecting the Sundarbans.
2827.statement: Everyone will have the same views and opinions about the importance of protecting the Sundarbans.
2827.correction: Role play could be used to investgate the perspectives of different stakeholders in the Sundarbans such as fishing communities, farmers, government officials, tourism operators and conservationists.

5707.belief: Population density is the same everywhere in India.
5707.statement: Population density is the same everywhere in India.
5707.correction: Population density varies across India; urban areas are densely populated, but rural areas, such as much of the Himalayas, are sparsely populated.

4605.belief: All migrants are forced to move.
4605.statement: All migrants are forced to move.
4605.correction: Explain that there are different reasons which can lead to someone migrating. These might be related to work, education, family, better services, living environment or safety. Spend time discussing these in more detail.

1945.belief: Confusion about the difference between global cities and megacities.
1945.statement: Confusion about the difference between global cities and megacities.
1945.correction: Global cities are well-connected cities that are recognised as being of global importance. Megacities are cities with more than 10 million inhabitants. Not all global cities are megacities.

4759.belief: Mumbai was only inhabited by people recently.
4759.statement: Mumbai was only inhabited by people recently.
4759.correction: People are thought to have first inhabited Mumbai in the Stone Age, hundreds of thousands of years ago.

3773.belief: Inequality is just about the difference in how much money people have.
3773.statement: Inequality is just about the difference in how much money people have.
3773.correction: There are many different inequalities between people’s lives such as access to education and health care, quality of housing, job opportunities and how people are treated.

2079.belief: A country is called a global superpower if it has a lot of money.
2079.statement: A country is called a global superpower if it has a lot of money.
2079.correction: A global superpower is used to describe a country that has a lot of power or influence over other countries and places in the world. Different factors make a global superpower powerful such as economic, cultural, population and resources.

2806.belief: Everyone is impacted by climate change equally.
2806.statement: Everyone is impacted by climate change equally.
2806.correction: Although everyone is affected by climate change, some people and places are impacted more than others.

1634.belief: China is about the same size as Greenland.
1634.statement: China is about the same size as Greenland.
1634.correction: China is around four times the size of Greenland although it looks about the same size on some projections of the world map.

5502.belief: The physical geography of China doesn't vary across the country.
5502.statement: The physical geography of China doesn't vary across the country.
5502.correction: China is a huge country with diverse landscapes and a range of biomes including desert, grassland, tropical forests and temperate forests.

2275.belief: Deserts are only found in very hot climates.
2275.statement: Deserts are only found in very hot climates.
2275.correction: Deserts are areas with extremely low rainfall and can be hot or cold depending on where they are located. The Gobi Desert is a cold desert.

5706.belief: Population density is the same everywhere in China.
5706.statement: Population density is the same everywhere in China.
5706.correction: Population density varies across China; urban areas such as Shanghai are densely populated, but rural areas, such as the mountainous regions covering much of western China, are sparsely populated.

598.belief: Beijing was only inhabited by people recently.
598.statement: Beijing was only inhabited by people recently.
598.correction: People are thought to have inhabited the area around Beijing since the Stone Age, hundreds of thousands of years ago.

2834.belief: Everything made in China is exported to other countries.
2834.statement: Everything made in China is exported to other countries.
2834.correction: China manufactures products for people to buy and use in China and countries around the world.

2795.belief: Everyone in China and around the world is equally responsible for climate change.
2795.statement: Everyone in China and around the world is equally responsible for climate change.
2795.correction: Although everyone has a carbon footprint, some people and places contribute more to climate change than others.

3323.belief: Globalisation is the world becoming more developed.
3323.statement: Globalisation is the world becoming more developed.
3323.correction: Globalisation is the world becoming more interconnected.

3909.correction: Jeans come from many different places.

10056.belief: Supply chains start at the manufacturing stage.
10056.statement: Supply chains start at the manufacturing stage.
10056.correction: Supply chains start when raw materials have been taken from the earth.

3324.belief: Globalisation is about the world developing.
3324.statement: Globalisation is about the world developing.
3324.correction: Globalisation is about the world becoming more connected.

10366.correction: You can trade goods and services such as education and finance services.

5274.belief: Most of our imports in the UK come from China.
5274.statement: Most of our imports in the UK come from China.
5274.correction: Most of our imports in the UK come from the US and EU countries.

10041.belief: The Suez Canal is only important for the Middle East.
10041.statement: The Suez Canal is only important for the Middle East.
10041.correction: The Suez Canal is important globally as 30% of all global container traffic and 12% of all global trade passes through the canal.

10344.belief: TNCs sell the same products in different countries.
10344.statement: TNCs sell the same products in different countries.
10344.correction: TNCs can sell different products in different countries.

4231.belief: Living standards and quality of life are the same.
4231.statement: Living standards and quality of life are the same.
4231.correction: Living standards are about the the level of necessities and comforts of daily life that is available to and affordable by a person.

11126.belief: All of the world is equally interconnected.
11126.statement: All of the world is equally interconnected.
11126.correction: Some parts of the world are more interconnected than others. It is influenced by many factors including wealth and size.

3320.belief: Globalisation is only beneficial to large companies.
3320.statement: Globalisation is only beneficial to large companies.
3320.correction: Globalisation can improve the quality of life of people.

10982.belief: Western culture refers to only North America.
10982.statement: Western culture refers to only North America.
10982.correction: Western culture refers to North America, Europe and Australia.

3240.belief: Geological timescales go back as far as human history.
3240.statement: Geological timescales go back as far as human history.
3240.correction: Geological timescales are much greater than human history.

5168.belief: There is only one type of rock, and rocks can't change.
5168.statement: There is only one type of rock, and rocks can't change.
5168.correction: Students will explore the three main types of rock found on Earth, and understand how rocks are recycled through the rock cycle.

10509.belief: The UK doesn't experience volcanic activity today, so volcanoes are not important to the UK's geological history.
10509.statement: The UK doesn't experience volcanic activity today, so volcanoes are not important to the UK's geological history.
10509.correction: The UK was once a volcanically active region due to its position near tectonic plate boundaries millions of years ago. Evidence of past volcanic activity includes: the Giant’s Causeway in Northern Ireland and the volcanic rocks in Snowdonia.

8988.belief: All rocks formed during the same geological period will be similar.
8988.statement: All rocks formed during the same geological period will be similar.
8988.correction: Although many rocks formed during the same geological period will be similar, volcanic processes may be creating rocks at the same time as sedimentary rocks are being created. These rocks will be very different and create contrasting landscapes.

10964.belief: Weathering and erosion are the same process.
10964.statement: Weathering and erosion are the same process.
10964.correction: Weathering breaks down rocks in place without movement, while erosion involves the removal and transport of that material by wind, water, ice, or gravity.

9876.belief: Grykes and clints are type of rock, rather than being a feature of limestone landscapes.
9876.statement: Some students may think that grykes and clints are type of rock, rather than being a feature of limestone landscapes.
9876.correction: Students will be taught what clints and grykes are in relation to limestone.

9398.correction: Soil is a complex and vital resource made of minerals, organic matter, water, and living organisms. It is important for growing food, storing carbon, and maintaining ecosystems. Without healthy soil, agriculture and natural habitats wouldn't survive.

4030.belief: Large soil particles means there are smaller pores between them.
4030.statement: Large soil particles means there are smaller pores between them.
4030.correction: Soil that is made-up of small particles has a structure where the particles can fit together more easily reducing the pore size between them.

5882.belief: Proportional data can only be presented using a pie chart.
5882.statement: Proportional data can only be presented using a pie chart.
5882.correction: A pie chart is by far the most common method that geographers use, but any shape can be split into proportional sections.

316.belief: Anomalous data can be ignored in the data analysis stage as it is due to human error in the data collection stage.
316.statement: Anomalous data can be ignored in the data analysis stage as it is due to human error in the data collection stage.
316.correction: Geographers will always try to find explanations for data that does not fit the general trend before they dismiss it as being caused by human error during the data collection stage.

9694.belief: Mass movement only occurs in mountainous areas or during extreme weather events.
9694.statement: Students may believe that mass movement only occurs in mountainous areas or during extreme weather events.
9694.correction: Mass movement can happen anywhere there are slopes, even in places with mild weather conditions. While extreme weather can trigger events, even light rainfall can cause mass movement if the slope is steep or the material is already weathered.

9037.belief: If we run out of oil, we can just make more.
9037.statement: If we run out of oil, we can just make more.
9037.correction: Fossil fuels take millions of years to form – much longer than a human lifetime. We can’t just “make” more. Once we use them up, they’re gone. That’s why we need to balance using them with finding cleaner, renewable alternatives.

3239.belief: Geological resources are all bad because they damage the environment.
3239.statement: Geological resources are all bad because they damage the environment.
3239.correction: While they can cause environmental harm, they also provide essential materials and economic benefits. The key is understanding both advantages and disadvantages—which is what geographers evaluate.

2558.belief: Earthquakes and volcanoes happen on tectonic plates.
2558.statement: Earthquakes and volcanoes happen on tectonic plates.
2558.correction: Tectonic plates cover the whole world, this would mean they happen everywhere. The majority of earthquakes and volcanoes occur at plate boundaries (where two plates meet), though there are some which happen away from boundaries.

9462.belief: South America and the South American plate are the same thing.
9462.statement: South America and the South American plate are the same thing.
9462.correction: South America is a continent (land), whereas the South American plate also includes part of the Atlantic ocean.

5062.belief: The oceanic plate subducts at a destructive plate margin and melts to form magma.
5062.statement: The oceanic plate subducts at a destructive plate margin and melts to form magma.
5062.correction: The water in the oceanic plate lowers the melting point, helping mantle rocks above to melt and form magma, not the subducting plate itself.

4047.belief: Lava and magma can be used interchangeably.
4047.statement: Lava and magma can be used interchangeably.
4047.correction: Magma is molten rock underground, whereas lava is molten rock above Earth's surface.

4046.belief: Lava is the only dangerous aspect to a volcanic eruption and you can just run out of the way.
4046.statement: Lava is the only dangerous aspect to a volcanic eruption and you can just run out of the way.
4046.correction: Ash, lahars and pyroclastic flows are all extremely dangerous volcanic hazards. Pyroclastic flows can reach speeds of 435 mph, which is faster than a car.

5415.belief: People do not live on volcanoes because it is too dangerous.
5415.statement: People do not live on volcanoes because it is too dangerous.
5415.correction: One in twenty people live close to an active volcano, as there are many attractive qualities to living there, e.g. fertile soils, tourist income and geothermal energy.

5570.belief: There are no plate boundaries in Africa.
5570.statement: There are no plate boundaries in Africa.
5570.correction: Mount Nyiragongo is on a constructive plate boundary known as the East African Rift System, where the African plate is splitting into the Nubian and Somali plates.

5571.belief: Plate boundaries are clean cuts through the ground which separate two plates.
5571.statement: Plate boundaries are clean cuts through the ground which separate two plates.
5571.correction: There is not one fault but many, which make up a plate boundary and the rock is locked together across the two plates.

2171.belief: A dangerous earthquake event is when the ground shakes, once. Then the danger is over.
2171.statement: A dangerous earthquake event is when the ground shakes, once. Then the danger is over.
2171.correction: Further sizeable earthquakes may occur in the days, weeks and months after a big earthquake, known as aftershocks, and these can be as dangerous for people and property, especially given the damage already done.

2554.belief: Earthquakes can be predicted a few weeks or days before they happen so that people can evacuate.
2554.statement: Earthquakes can be predicted a few weeks or days before they happen so that people can evacuate.
2554.correction: Humans can calculate the probability of an earthquake happening within a region, over a long period of time. It is not possible to predict exactly when or where earthquakes will occur, or of what size.

9426.belief: If someone survives and is not injured during the earthquake, they are then safe.
9426.statement: If someone survives and is not injured during the earthquake, they are then safe.
9426.correction: Since many survivors had to stay in crowded shelters or sleep outside, the risk of diseases increased. In addition, strong aftershocks hit the area, damaging buildings that were already unstable.

10456.correction: Tsunamis are caused by displacement of the ocean, not wind blowing over the surface. Tsunami waves don’t break, they come as a fast-moving wall of water, which can be far bigger and faster than a normal wave. They can also flood kilometres inland.

2805.belief: Everyone in high-income countries in the UK is wealthier than people in low-income countries like Kenya.
2805.statement: Everyone in high-income countries in the UK is wealthier than people in low-income countries like Kenya.
2805.correction: The average income in the UK is higher than in Kenya, but there is a big variation in both countries. There are very wealthy people in Kenya and people on very low incomes in the UK.

3774.belief: Inequality just refers to the uneven distribution of wealth.
3774.statement: Inequality just refers to the uneven distribution of wealth.
3774.correction: Inequality is about more than wealth. It is the uneven distribution of resources, opportunities, and living conditions. It includes different categories such as economic, political, social, environmental and digital.

3217.belief: GDP per capita is the most effective way to measure development.
3217.statement: GDP per capita is the most effective way to measure development.
3217.correction: Although useful, GDP per capita is not as effective as composite indicators such as HDI, which include a measure of health and education

2072.belief: Countries with the highest GDP per capita always have the highest healthy life expectancy.
2072.statement: Countries with the highest GDP per capita always have the highest healthy life expectancy.
2072.correction: This isn't always the case as other factors also play a big role, like access to healthcare, lifestyle, diet, pollution levels, and inequality.

8698.belief: The quality of life of people around the world is getting worse.
8698.statement: The quality of life of people around the world is getting worse.
8698.correction: In most places around the world, social indicators such as life expectancy and the average expected years of schooling, have increased.

2577.belief: Economic development can be fully explained by physical geography.
2577.statement: Economic development can be fully explained by physical geography.
2577.correction: Physical geography is one factor in influencing a country’s development. Other factors such as history and politics often have a greater influence.

3501.belief: Historical factors no longer impact on global inequality around the world.
3501.statement: Historical factors no longer impact on global inequality around the world.
3501.correction: There is an enduring impact of history on global inequality. Historical factors have shaped wealth, opportunities, and power today.

5405.belief: Most people who have to flee their home due to war will travel a long distance away from their country.
5405.statement: Most people who have to flee their home due to war will travel a long distance away from their country.
5405.correction: Although some refugees will travel a long distance, most people who have to leave quickly for their own safety will travel to a neighbouring country.

3221.belief: Gender inequality is the same around the world.
3221.statement: Gender inequality is the same around the world.
3221.correction: Gender inequality varies around the world.

1633.belief: China produces the most greenhouse gases per capita in the world.
1633.statement: China produces the most greenhouse gases per capita in the world.
1633.correction: China produces the most greenhouse gases in the world, but with a population of over 1.4 billion people, their per capita emissions are significantly lower than many other countries.

2315.belief: Development is always driven by governments and big international organisations.
2315.statement: Development is always driven by governments and big international organisations.
2315.correction: While governments and organisations play a big role, development often happens through smaller, community-led projects where local people take charge.

3386.belief: Grassroots development was invented by western thinkers.
3386.statement: Grassroots development was invented by western thinkers.
3386.correction: In reality, many communities around the world have practiced grassroots development for centuries, using their own knowledge and solutions before Western ideas became popular.

10563.belief: Urbanisation only happens in rich countries.
10563.statement: Urbanisation only happens in rich countries.
10563.correction: Urbanisation is occurring fastest in low and middle income countries due to rapid population growth and rural to urban migration

1673.belief: Cities are growing at the same rate everywhere around the world.
1673.statement: Cities are growing at the same rate everywhere around the world.
1673.correction: Cities are growing at different rates around the world. Often, cities in countries with a lower HDI are growing more rapidly than cities in countries with a higher HDI.

1672.belief: Cities grow randomly without any structure or planning.
1672.statement: Cities grow randomly without any structure or planning.
1672.correction: In reality, urban land use is often influenced by models (like the Burgess or Hoyt models), and factors such as history, economics, transport links, and the environment shape how cities develop and function over time.

4545.belief: All megacities are global cities because they are so big.
4545.statement: All megacities are global cities because they are so big.
4545.correction: Not all megacities are global cities. While megacities have populations of over 10 million, global cities are defined by their international influence in areas such as finance, culture, politics, and transport.

1671.belief: Cities only grow because of migration.
1671.statement: Cities only grow because of migration.
1671.correction: While migration is a key factor, natural increase (more births than deaths) is often just as important - especially in cities with young populations.

4229.belief: Living in cities only means dealing with problems like noise and crowds.
4229.statement: Living in cities only means dealing with problems like noise and crowds.
4229.correction: While cities can have challenges like noise and crowds, they also offer many benefits such as better jobs, healthcare, education, cultural events, and opportunities to meet people from different backgrounds.

9218.belief: Services grow at the same pace as population in cities.
9218.statement: Services grow at the same pace as population in cities.
9218.correction: When the population of a city grows rapidly, often the growth of services is slower. In the twenty-first century this is particularly the case in rapidly developing countries, where lots of people arrive into cities each year.

10562.belief: Urban regeneration only means building new houses.
10562.statement: Urban regeneration only means building new houses.
10562.correction: Regeneration is not just about new housing—it also improves transport, creates jobs, and provides community services.

3764.belief: All industrial cities decline once their factories close.
3764.statement: All industrial cities decline once their factories close.
3764.correction: Some cities, like Sheffield, adapt by developing new industries, services, and cultural attractions after industrial decline.

653.belief: Only big cities in rich countries cause climate change.
653.statement: Only big cities in rich countries cause climate change.
653.correction: Cities of all sizes, in both rich and poorer countries, contribute to climate change through emissions, especially from transport, energy use, and waste.

10075.belief: Sustainability is only about protecting the environment.
10075.statement: Sustainability is only about protecting the environment.
10075.correction: Sustainability also includes improving people’s lives and meeting their needs fairly.

1670.belief: Cities can’t do much to stop climate change because it’s a global problem.
1670.statement: Cities can’t do much to stop climate change because it’s a global problem.
1670.correction: While climate change is a global issue, cities can make a big difference by reducing emissions and adapting their infrastructure to protect people and the environment.

2502.belief: The DRC is a relatively small country.
2502.statement: The DRC is a relatively small country.
2502.correction: The DRC is a very large country. It's position on the equator means that it often appears smaller than it really is on some world maps.

5709.belief: Population pyramids only show us the total population size.
5709.statement: Population pyramids only show us the total population size.
5709.correction: A population pyramid provides information about the structure of the population; the age and gender profile of the location represented. This can help governments with future planning.

2077.belief: Countries are always the same shape and size, with the same borders and the same name throughout their history and that these aspects will never change.
2077.statement: That countries are always the same shape and size, with the same borders and the same name throughout their history and that these aspects will never change.
2077.correction: History has shown that in many countries borders move, countries expand or shrink and the name of any given country is not fixed and permanent. These things are often the result of conflict or warfare which causes significant political change.

3545.belief: Housing in cities is better / bigger / cheaper / more available than in rural areas.
3545.statement: That housing in cities is better / bigger / cheaper / more available than in rural areas.
3545.correction: Cities are often perceived to have better or more housing but this is not always the case. Inner city housing can be small and run down; people who move to cities may not find accomodation at all and may have to live in informal settlements.

5525.belief: Places which experience rain, particularly heavy rain as in the DRC, musn't experience water scarcity or drought.
5525.statement: That places which experience rain, particularly heavy rain as in the DRC, musn't experience water scarcity or drought.
5525.correction: Heavy rainfall is experienced in some parts of the DRC such as rainforests whilst other parts such as savanna are very dry. Furthermore rainforests are depleting and savanna is expanding as global temperatures are rising, increasing risks of drought.

2240.belief: The Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring country, the Republic of Congo, are the same country. Students can inadvertently shorten DRC to 'Congo' in verbal or written work.
2240.statement: That the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring country, the Republic of Congo, are the same country. Students can inadvertently shorten DRC to 'Congo' in verbal or written work.
2240.correction: The DRC and the Republic of Congo are two separate countries in central Africa. The Congo River forms part of the border between the countries; their capital cities Kinshasa and Brazzaville are located on oppposite banks of the river from each other.

1964.belief: The Congo rainforest is only found in the DRC.
1964.statement: That the Congo rainforest is only found in the DRC.
1964.correction: The Congo rainforest is found in the Congo Basin, which spans six countries in Africa: Cameroon, Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.

5619.belief: Poaching only involves 'trophy' animals like elephants and wild cats.
5619.statement: That poaching only involves 'trophy' animals like elephants and wild cats.
5619.correction: Poaching happens on a daily basis all around the world as a means of organised illegal activity (but in some cases for survival). It can include any animal species, large or small, that has a perceived value in its meat, skin, or another biproduct.

4837.belief: All natural resources are found deep underground and so need to be mined to extract them.
4837.statement: That all natural resources are found deep underground and so need to be mined to extract them.
4837.correction: Some natural resources are found deep underground, like ores of some metals and fossil fuels. Others are not found underground, for example the rainforest trees that are used for timber or as a source of rubber, or water sources like lakes.

2221.belief: Deforestation and logging are the same thing.
2221.statement: That deforestation and logging are the same thing.
2221.correction: Logging is the use of trees as a natural resource for their wood and can happen legally or illegaly. Deforestation is the cutting down of trees for many reasons, often to make space for other activities such as mining, road building or farming.

3656.belief: The most important rainforest to protect is the Amazon and that other rainforests are smaller so they don't matter as much.
3656.statement: That the most important rainforest to protect is the Amazon and that other rainforests are smaller so they don't matter as much.
3656.correction: Tropical rainforests are rich in biodiversity and play a crucial role in regulating Earth's climate as carbon sinks. Rainforests in Africa or Asia are as important as the Amazon in South America, so global climate action is needed to protect them.

3352.belief: The government of the DRC is only concerned with the military and defence and not with other important matters that affect the people.
3352.statement: That the government of the DRC is only concerned with the military and defence and not with other important matters that affect the people.
3352.correction: The government of the DRC has many departments focussed on a variety of areas from energy and industries to farming and conservation. The government makes policies and pledges in a number of contexts, not only in defence and military matters.

4951.belief: Nigeria is a relatively small country.
4951.statement: Nigeria is a relatively small country.
4951.correction: Nigeria is a relatively large country. It is much bigger than France despite it looking a similar size on some map projections.

5504.belief: The physical geography of Nigeria is very similar everywhere in the country.
5504.statement: The physical geography of Nigeria is very similar everywhere in the country.
5504.correction: Nigeria has a range of physical features. These include rivers, plateaux, mountains, savannas, deserts and coastlines.

4230.belief: Living conditions are always better in urban areas than rural areas.
4230.statement: Living conditions are always better in urban areas than rural areas.
4230.correction: There is a wide variety of living conditions within, as well as between, rural and urban communities.

4007.belief: Lagos is the capital of Nigeria.
4007.statement: Lagos is the capital of Nigeria.
4007.correction: Lagos became the capital of an independent Nigeria in 1960 but was replaced by Abuja in 1991.

912.belief: The challenges facing Lagos aren’t problems in other cities.
912.statement: The challenges facing Lagos aren’t problems in other cities.
912.correction: Many of the challenges facing Lagos are issues in most of the world’s cities.

2818.belief: Everyone in Nigeria has similar viewpoints about the future of the country’s oil industry.
2818.statement: Everyone in Nigeria has similar viewpoints about the future of the country’s oil industry.
2818.correction: People are connected to the oil industry in Nigeria in different ways. Different stakeholders often have different ideas and opinions about what the future of Nigeria’s oil industry should look like.

2817.belief: Everyone in Nigeria is impacted by climate change equally.
2817.statement: Everyone in Nigeria is impacted by climate change equally.
2817.correction: Some people in Nigeria are impacted by climate change more than than others. Many different overlapping factors make some people more vulnerable to climate change impacts than others.

382.belief: Around one quarter of water is found on land.
382.statement: Around one quarter of water is found on land.
382.correction: Only 0.9% of water is stored on land.

5158.belief: There is one source to a river.
5158.statement: There is one source to a river.
5158.correction: There can be many different sources within a drainage basin system.

496.belief: Attrition is where rocks and sediment carried by the river collide with the bed and the banks causing pieces to break off.
496.statement: Attrition is where rocks and sediment carried by the river collide with the bed and the banks causing pieces to break off.
496.correction: Abrasion is where rocks and sediment carried by the river collide with the bed and the banks causing pieces to break off.

8971.belief: A river has the most energy in the upper course.
8971.statement: A river has the most energy in the upper course.
8971.correction: The river does not have that much energy in the upper course as there is not a lot of water in the river.

4129.correction: Levees can be built as a flood defence but they can also be created naturally.

2963.belief: Field sketches are artistic impressions of a geographical scene.
2963.statement: Field sketches are artistic impressions of a geographical scene.
2963.correction: Field sketches are about clearly representing the geographical features of a place, not about the artistic skills of the geographer.

5674.belief: Points in a channel profile should be joined using a ruler.
5674.statement: Points in a channel profile should be joined using a ruler.
5674.correction: Points in a channel profile should be drawn with a slight curve to more accurately represent the shape of the river channel.

275.belief: The angle of the line of best fit tells geographers how strong the correlation is between two variables.
275.statement: The angle of the line of best fit tells geographers how strong the correlation is between two variables.
275.correction: The strength of the correlation is decided by how close the plots are to the line of best fit.

3051.belief: Flooding is only caused by physical factors such as heavy rainfall.
3051.statement: Flooding is only caused by physical factors such as heavy rainfall.
3051.correction: Human factors can lead to flooding too, such as deforestation.

3054.correction: Flooding is a natural process; it can have positive environmental effects, such as soil replenishment.

3053.belief: Flooding only happens close to rivers.
3053.statement: Flooding only happens close to rivers.
3053.correction: Flooding can also happen away from rivers, especially after heavy rainfall. When the ground can't absorb the water fast enough, surface water builds up and causes floods — even in places far from rivers.

3448.belief: Hard engineering is always very effective at protecting from flooding.
3448.statement: Hard engineering is always very effective at protecting from flooding.
3448.correction: Channel straightening, dredging and embankments can all make flooding worse downstream, as the channel can hold more water and speed up the flow.

3359.belief: Only governments help make decisions on where flood protection is used.
3359.statement: Only governments help make decisions on where flood protection is used.
3359.correction: Many stakeholders are invloved in making decisions on flood defences.

4838.belief: All natural resources are natural and untouched by humans.
4838.statement: All natural resources are natural and untouched by humans.
4838.correction: Many natural resources have been heavily managed, modified, or even created by humans, such as: managed forests, fish farms, or reservoirs.

5006.belief: Nuclear energy is either a renewable source of energy or a fossil fuel.
5006.statement: Nuclear energy is either a renewable source of energy or a fossil fuel.
5006.correction: Nuclear energy is a non-renewable energy source but is not a fossil fuel.

2665.belief: Any energy source can be produced anywhere.
2665.statement: Any energy source can be produced anywhere.
2665.correction: Human and physical geography must be considered when locating energy sources.

11018.belief: Wind farms are best located as remotely as possible.
11018.statement: Wind farms are best located as remotely as possible.
11018.correction: Wind farms should be located far from densely populated areas but close to the electricity grid. If they are too remote, the cost of connecting them to the grid will be high.

5600.belief: There are plenty more fish in the sea.
5600.statement: There are plenty more fish in the sea.
5600.correction: In 2018, nearly 90% of the world’s marine (sea) fish stocks were fully exploited, overexploited or depleted.

2146.belief: Customer decisions don’t make a difference to global fish populations.
2146.statement: Customer decisions don’t make a difference to global fish populations.
2146.correction: Eating fish from well-managed fisheries helps prevent overfishing, protects marine biodiversity, and ensures fish populations remain healthy for future generations.

5736.belief: It is not possible to be overweight and undernourished at the same time.
5736.statement: It is not possible to be overweight and undernourished at the same time.
5736.correction: Undernourishment occurs when someone isn’t receiving enough calories or essential nutrients to grow and function well. So it is possible to over eat but not eat enough of the right foods to acquire sufficient nutrients.

10200.belief: All the tests run on GM crops have found that they create no health issues.
10200.statement: All the tests run on GM crops have found that they create no health issues.
10200.correction: Most major scientific bodies find no conclusive evidence of harm from approved GM foods, which have all been tested. However, some animal studies raise questions, and critics argue that long-term human studies are limited.

3565.belief: Hydroponic and aquaponic systems are completely self-sustaining or maintenance-free.
3565.statement: Hydroponic and aquaponic systems are completely self-sustaining or maintenance-free.
3565.correction: Require regular monitoring, energy inputs and human intervention to stay productive.

717.belief: Boycotting palm oil helps stop deforestation.
717.statement: Boycotting palm oil helps stop deforestation.
717.correction: Experts recommend supporting certified sustainable palm oil, as palm oil is the most land-efficient oil crop. Replacing it with less efficient crops like sunflowers could cause more deforestation.

4582.belief: Methane from cow flatulence causes global warming.
4582.statement: Methane from cow flatulence causes global warming.
4582.correction: Ruminant animals (like cows and sheep) produce methane during digestion, 90–95% of this is released through eructation (burping). Methane is a greenhouse gas, which insulates our planet.

8756.correction: Despite their name, they’re not actually rare in quantity, they’re just rarely found in concentrated, economically viable deposits.

8978.belief: Rivers can't flow through areas with very low rainfall totals.
8978.statement: Rivers can't flow through areas with very low rainfall totals.
8978.correction: Rivers often flow through different climate zones, therefore their source may be in a mountainous area with high rainfall totals, but they may then flow through arid areas to the sea.

4595.belief: The Middle East is all desert.
4595.statement: The Middle East is all desert.
4595.correction: The Middle East is so vast that it contains a number of different biomes.

4596.belief: The Middle East is all desert and has no rivers.
4596.statement: The Middle East is all desert and has no rivers.
4596.correction: Students will explore the Tigris and Euphrates and understand how they created ancient civilisations and continue to support farming today.

4597.belief: All Middle Eastern countries are rich because they have oil.
4597.statement: All Middle Eastern countries are rich because they have oil.
4597.correction: While oil is a major resource, not every country has it. Countries like Yemen and Jordan have little or no oil, which affects their economies differently.

2813.belief: Everyone in the Middle East lives in the desert.
2813.statement: Everyone in the Middle East lives in the desert.
2813.correction: Although deserts cover a vast amount of land, people tend to cluster around water sources like rivers and coasts. That’s why cities like Cairo (near the Nile) are densely populated.

4616.belief: All migration in the Middle East is forced due to conflict.
4616.statement: All migration in the Middle East is forced due to conflict.
4616.correction: While war and displacement are significant in parts of the Middle East, the region is also a major destination for voluntary economic migration, especially to the Gulf States like the UAE, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia.

1652.belief: Christianity is the oldest religion that originated in the Middle East.
1652.statement: Christianity is the oldest religion that originated in the Middle East.
1652.correction: Judaism is almost 2000 years older than Christianity.

2524.belief: Dubai is only rich because of oil.
2524.statement: Dubai is only rich because of oil.
2524.correction: Whilst oil funded Dubai’s early growth, it now contributes only a small part of its GDP. Tourism, finance, and trade are the dominant economic drivers today.

814.belief: Camels store water in their humps.
814.statement: Camels store water in their humps.
814.correction: Camels store fat in their humps for energy, not water.

824.belief: We cannot grow new plants in the desert, it is too dry.
824.statement: We cannot grow new plants in the desert, it is too dry.
824.correction: Plants can have special features, or adaptations, to help them survive in the desert. This, alongside new technology, means that plants can sustain life in the desert and overcome the issue of desertification.

4594.belief: The Middle East is already hot and dry, so climate change won’t really affect it.
4594.statement: The Middle East is already hot and dry, so climate change won’t really affect it.
4594.correction: Climate change will continue to make the region hotter and drier, which will have consequences such as desertification, water scarcity and food shortages.

5133.belief: There has only been one ice age.
5133.statement: There has only been one ice age.
5133.correction: There have been numerous periods of warming and cooling throughout Earth's history. This has meant there have been a number of ice ages throughout history.

3314.belief: Glaciers are made of salt water.
3314.statement: Glaciers are made of salt water
3314.correction: Glaciers are made of fresh water from snow and rain

3315.correction: Glaciers can appear dirty because they carry material.

10446.belief: Truncated spurs are created soley by glaciers.
10446.statement: Truncated spurs are created soley by glaciers.
10446.correction: Truncated spurs started as interlocking spurs which are a fluvial feature formed by rivers. Glaciers then modify this landform through erosion.

4008.belief: The Lake District only has lakes.
4008.statement: The Lake District only has lakes.
4008.correction: While famous for its lakes, the region also features mountains, forests, and valleys, including England’s highest peak, Scafell Pike.

10359.belief: Tourism at the Mer de Glace only has negative impacts.
10359.statement: Tourism at the Mer de Glace only has negative impacts.
10359.correction: Tourism at the Mer de Glace has both positive and negative impacts. Positive impacts include boosts to the local economy and an awareness of climate change.

331.belief: Antarctica is an ocean covered in ice.
331.statement: Antarctica is an ocean covered in ice.
331.correction: Antarctica is a continent, not an ocean. It has a landmass beneath its thick ice sheets, unlike the Arctic, which is sea ice floating on the ocean.

3084.correction: A food web is not linear, it is complex and interconnected.

332.belief: Antarctica is owned by a group of countries.
332.statement: Antarctica is owned by a group of countries.
332.correction: Antarctica is one of the global commons, meaning it belongs to all of humanity, not individual nations.

366.correction: Approximately 4 million people live in the Arctic region.

295.belief: Animals in the Arctic are camouflaged with white fur all year round.
295.statement: Animals in the Arctic are camouflaged with white fur all year round.
295.correction: The Arctic fox is camouflaged with white fur in winter and brown fur in summer.

4552.belief: Melting sea ice does not impact ocean currents.
4552.statement: Melting sea ice does not impact ocean currents.
4552.correction: Melting ice alters the balance of freshwater and saltwater in the ocean, which can disrupt major ocean currents like the Gulf Stream.

1719.belief: The climate of Russia is always cold.
1719.statement: The climate of Russia is always cold.
1719.correction: The climate of Russia varies across its territory and across the year.

9045.belief: Russia is entirely a harsh, cold, mountainous, barren landscape.
9045.statement: That Russia is entirely a harsh, cold, mountainous, barren landscape.
9045.correction: Some parts of Russia do experience a harsh environment, but Russia is the largest country in the world by area, and so it has a diverse range of environments within it from mountains and volcanoes to vast plains and mighty rivers.

2898.belief: Each factor can be viewed independently.
2898.statement: Each factor can be viewed independently.
2898.correction: To understand the climate of a place or when comparing the climates of places, the factors need to be considered collectively and each factor may have a different level of relevance.

2264.belief: When describing patterns of distribution from maps pupils can make the mistake of including information not available on the map itself and get tempted to explain patterns.
2264.statement: When describing patterns of distribution from maps pupils can make the mistake of including information not available on the map itself and get tempted to explain patterns.
2264.correction: Use only the available information to write a description of what you see on the map including the general pattern and specific details provided by the legend, labels, compass rose and scale.

10169.belief: Temperate grasslands are the only places in the world where cereal crops are grown.
10169.statement: Temperate grasslands are the only places in the world where cereal crops are grown.
10169.correction: Whilst temperate grasslands are significant providers of much of the world’s wheat and other cereal crops and referred to as 'breadbaskets', they are not the only places in the world where these crops are grown.

6735.statement: Pupils often get the command language of describe and explain mixed up, most often causing them to explain something when just a description has been asked for.
6735.correction: A description gives details of what something is like. It should contain as much detail as possible. An explanation gives reasons for the features and should use langauge such as 'because', 'as a result of', 'due to'.

9046.belief: Russia and the USSR are the same.
9046.statement: Russia and the USSR are the same.
9046.correction: Russia was the largest part of the USSR, but they are not the same. The USSR was a union of 15 republics, including Russia. It dissolved in 1991, and each republic, like Ukraine and Georgia, became independent.

4722.correction: Moscow is not representative of all of Russia; life in other regions can be very different. Moscow is the richest and most developed part of the country and other regions vary in terms of culture, economy, and infrastructure.

6932.statement: Pupils can make sweeping statements about people that live in places.
6932.correction: It is important that data is used as an average and not the characteristics of every individual. The word stereotype is useful to use in this instance.

7583.statement: Pupils can have a tendency to think about the immediate impacts and not consider those over longer stretches of time.
7583.correction: Geographers need to think about diffferent dimensions of time i.e. short term and long term and use this as a framework to support understanding and evaluation.

10053.belief: A superpower only refers to a country's military power and influence.
10053.statement: A superpower only refers to a country's military power and influence.
10053.correction: Superpower status depends on a country's economy, population, military, energy reserves and cultural power.

9044.belief: Russia will benefit from climate change because it will make the country warmer, allowing for more agriculture and economic opportunities.
9044.statement: Russia will benefit from climate change because it will make the country warmer, allowing for more agriculture and economic opportunities.
9044.correction: While warming may open up some land for agriculture, the negative impacts will outweigh potential benefits. For example, flooding and unpredictable weather patterns will harm crops and water supplies.

334.belief: The Anthropocene is the period of Earth’s history from when homosapiens first evolved.
334.statement: The Anthropocene is the period of Earth’s history from when homosapiens first evolved.
334.correction: The Anthropocene is a proposed geological epoch that marks the period in Earth’s history during which human activity has had a significant impact on Earth.

4593.belief: Microplastics are only found in the ocean.
4593.statement: Microplastics are only found in the ocean.
4593.correction: Microplastics are found in the ocean, soil, rock and animals.

3851.belief: Invasive species are always introduced by humans intentionally.
3851.statement: Invasive species are always introduced by humans intentionally.
3851.correction: While some introductions are intentional (e.g. for pest control or landscaping), many invasive species are introduced accidentally, such as via ballast water in ships or hitchhiking on imported goods.

3685.belief: Incinerarting waste is good for the environment.
3685.statement: Incinerarting waste is good for the environment.
3685.correction: Incinerating waste releases toxic gases and carbon emissions.

5569.belief: Plastic will eventually biodegrade, even if it takes hundreds of years.
5569.statement: Plastic will eventually biodegrade, even if it takes hundreds of years.
5569.correction: Plastic is not biodegradable, it just breaks down into smaller and smaller pieces and eventually turns into microplastics (tiny plastic pieces, smaller than 5 mm).

5061.belief: Ocean acidification is when water is polluted from human activities on land.
5061.statement: Ocean acidification is when water is polluted from human activities on land.
5061.correction: Ocean acidification is when the ocean absorbs extra carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the air, which makes the water more acidic.

9160.belief: Secondary data has to have been collected by an expert in the data and the topic area.
9160.statement: Secondary data has to have been collected by an expert in the data and the topic area.
9160.correction: Though geographers often use secondary data that has been researched and produced by experts, it does not have to be: it can come from other students.

1765.belief: The colours geographers use in their data presentation are always randomly chosen.
1765.statement: The colours geographers use in their data presentation are always randomly chosen.
1765.correction: The colours geographers use are often associated with social conventions such as red being negative and green being positive.

3337.belief: You have to be good at maths to be able to use statistical tests in geographical enquiries.
3337.statement: You have to be good at maths to be able to use statistical tests in geographical enquiries.
